doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The player piano, radio and dancing aunties
summary: The family had a player piano and a radio rather than records; Liston pedalled it while her aunties danced.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: At your home, I know you said you had a piano – a piano-roll piano. So you were exposed to that. And you had a radio, and you were exposed to the music that you heard that was being played around Kansas City. And also, your grandfather listened to – did he have records or something?
No. We didn’t have records at that time. We had the player. This is my – this is the same piano.
But it had legs on it. It had really big feet – lovely feet on it. All that stuff.
Did you sit there and pedal it.
Yeah, and my aunties would dance.
But your mother? Did she dance too?
Nah. I don’t think so. I don’t remember her dancing.
